messages:
Morgan: quick dump — ran a stratified sweep on sm83 for INT4 vs FP8 kernels across seq_len 16/128/2048. attaching the short summary below, want opinions on per-arch workspace and kv-chunk thresholds.

Morgan: TL;DR: int4 wins at short/med sequences for throughput, but at 2048 we see FP8 kernels with better tail latency and less OOM risk. weird perf cliff around seq=1024 when kv cache splits.

Vikram: can you paste the config you used for the kernel picker?

Morgan: sure — config snippet I tested:
```
kernel_policy:
  - arch: sm83
    prefer: int4_fused_gemm_v1
    fallback: fp8_block_sparse
    workspace_mb: 320
    kv_chunk_size: 1024
    seq_switch: 900  # switch path for seq > 900
  - arch: sm86
    prefer: int4_wide_gemv
    fallback: int8_fallback
    workspace_mb: 256
    kv_chunk_size: 512
```

Rachel: that seq_switch entry is interesting. did you try dynamic kv chunking (reduce chunk when memory pressure rises)?

Morgan: yes — I tried adaptive kv_chunk: start 1024 then halve on mem>85%. helps, but at seq=2048 the int4 kernels still thrash L2 and cause stalls. FP8 avoids extra packing/unpacking and runs smoother.

Emily: numbers? small table pls (latency p95 in ms, mem MB).

Morgan: pasted logs below (abridged):
```
# sm83, batch=8
seq=16  int4 p95=12.3ms  mem=1.2GB
seq=128 int4 p95=34.8ms  mem=1.8GB
seq=1024 int4 p95=210.5ms mem=5.4GB  <-- cliff
seq=2048 int4 p95=520.1ms mem=9.1GB  OOM in some runs
seq=2048 fp8  p95=310.2ms mem=7.2GB  stable
```

Vikram: cliff at 1024 sounds like KV cache split + workspace reallocation. Are we doing full KV concat or incremental copy?

Morgan: current code concatenates and reserializes when chunk boundary crossed. that's the costly bit.

Josh: Can we change to a streaming append that maintains page-aligned buffers? avoid large memcpy spikes.

Morgan: I prototyped streaming KV append — reduces pause but increases steady-state memory by ~6%. net p95 improved for int4 at 1024 by ~35ms.

perf-bot: regression alert — int4_fused_gemm_v1 shows +18% p95 vs baseline at seq=512 on nightly runs. tagging @Vikram @Morgan

Vikram: seeing perf-bot — that aligns with me rolling sm83 kernel microchanges yesterday. I think the new tile-size heuristic went too aggressive for 512-1024.

Rachel: propose: revert tile heuristic for sm83, enable streaming KV append, and add a soft threshold to prefer fp8 for seq>=1500 by default. we can expose overrides per-customer.

Emily: +1. also add metric for memcpy spikes (count and duration) to Console so we can correlate.

Morgan: will implement revert + streaming kv + metric. also want to test reducing workspace_mb to 256 for sm83 to see if it forces better kernel variant selection earlier.

Josh: FYI, for Dedicated customers with pinned GPUs we might want a per-deployment profile that forces int4 even for long seqs if they'd rather trade mem for cost. add config flag: force_quant_preference.

Morgan: good call. I'll add config and run another sweep tomorrow.

infra-bot: scheduled perf sweep job #1775234-kwp starts at 2026-03-18T09:30Z. results will post here.

Vikram: thanks. after that we should produce a one-pager with recommended default policy per arch+seq band (sm83: int4 for <=1024 w/ streaming-kv; fp8 for >1024). but include caveat for batch sizes >16.

Rachel: agree. also file a small playbook for rollbacks if int4 changes reappear in perf-bot. :thumbsup:

Morgan: noted. I'll push the PR with revert + streaming KV + metric instrumentation and reference this thread.

perf-bot: job finished — summary: int4 p95 improved post-streaming-kv by 9% at seq=1024, fp8 still best at 2048. attaching artifacts location /artifacts/1775234/kv-streaming/

Morgan: perfect — thanks all. continuing in follow-up PR comments.
